reason: Probe t6 (run_claim_probe on the real kernel) demonstrated that the kernel's Smith-style algorithm violates the contract's componentwise tolerance abs(actual - target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| on legal FP16 inputs. Case A (numerator rows [1000,3000]/den [7,21] and [65504,65504]/den [3,-3], all finite FP16 values within the contract's declared domain) produced max abs error 6.51e-4 with an err/tolerance ratio of 12.77 — the true component is near zero due to cancellation while numerator terms are large, so the FP32-rounded `ratio` error is amplified far beyond tolerance. Control cases (subnormal inputs ratio 0.013, large-magnitude grid ratio 0.13) stayed within tolerance, isolating the failure to the ratio-rounding cancellation the kernel's tl.div_rn/tl.fma formulation produces. The contract explicitly requires every finite FP16 component combination to meet the per-component tolerance, so this is an in-scope required-behaviour violation.
